questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

As of now, they have finished the __construction of the ground flour.__
questions.solution:

• The correct substitution is option 2) **"construction of the ground floor".**
 
• The** sentence appears** to be discussing a construction project.
 
• **In this context,** the term **"ground floor"** is the most appropriate because it refers to the first or main level of a building.
 
• The original underlined word,** "flour",** is a typo.** It refers **to a type of food substance and does not fit in the context of construction.
 
• The other options "flavor", "flower", and "flounder" also don't fit the context because they do not have meanings related to building construction.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'As of now, they have finished the **construction of the ground floor.'***

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

__
 
• The correct substitution is option 4) **"was delighted".**
 
• The original sentence *"I was delight in the moment I saw her*" is **grammatically incorrect.**
 
• The phrase **"was delighted"** is the proper form for expressing that the speaker experienced a feeling of delight or pleasure.
 
• The word** "delighted**" is a past participle adjective that describes the speaker's state or feeling.

Therefore, the** correct sentence **is:* 'I was delighted in the moment I saw her.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 2) **"had delightful" **is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• Option 3) **"was delighting"** suggests an ongoing action rather than a state or feeling, which seems less likely given the context.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My aunt Geeta, / is knowing / my friend Rudransh / very well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **segment** that contains a grammatical **error** is **"is knowing".**
 
• In English, the verb **"know"** is a stative verb, not an action verb, meaning it describes a state or condition, not an action that is happening.
 
• Therefore, it's not typically used in the continuous tense. The** correct form **should be **"knows".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** would be: *"My aunt Geeta knows my friend Rudransh very well."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here's a brief explanation of the other options:
 
 
• **"Very well" **- This is an adverb phrase used to describe the extent of the verb. In this case, it's used to indicate the depth of knowledge or familiarity. There's no error here.
 
• **"My aunt Geeta" -** This is a proper noun phrase serving as the subject of the sentence. There's no error in this segment.
 
• **"My friend Rudransh" **- This is a noun phrase serving as the object of the sentence. Again, there's no error in this segment.
